title: Struggle is most severe between members of the same species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Struggle is most severe between members of the same species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The struggle for existence is almost always most severe between individuals of the same species, because they live in the same places, need the same food and face the same dangers; between varieties of a species it is nearly as severe.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But the struggle almost invariably will be most severe between the individuals of the same species, for they frequent the same districts, require the same food, and are exposed to the same dangers.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter III, “Struggle for Existence”; section “Struggle for life most severe between individuals and varieties of the same species; often severe between species of the same genus”. Scope: all organisms, including varieties of cultivated plants and domestic animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch03-11: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.56

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Competition coefficients are directly estimable, but no broad integrated public dataset compares all competitor classes across organisms. Meta-analysis of archived studies can test subsets with substantial harmonization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare per-capita fitness effects of increasing conspecific, same-species-variety and heterospecific density across replicated field or experimental communities. Consistently largest negative effects from conspecific density support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Natural enemies can generate apparent conspecific density dependence.

Comparable intra- and interspecific manipulations are sparse.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.73
analysis feasibility: 0.53
data existence: 0.63
data adequacy: 0.39
discriminating power: 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Intraspecific versus interspecific effect size is a standard and discriminating contrast, and plant-community datasets plus demographic models cover a real subset. The cleanest coefficients are still scattered, so a global 'almost always' ranking would mean harmonizing studies for weeks to months. Animals and domesticated varieties are the thin part of the scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the strength of intraspecific competition with interspecific competition, using per-capita effects from removal experiments, frequency dependence, or fitted competition coefficients. A general ranking of intraspecific effects as stronger, including among varieties, would support the statement; interspecific effects as strong or stronger in most pairs would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Varieties of domesticated organisms, included in the scope, are rarely in the same competition datasets as wild species.

Co-occurrence is a poor proxy for the severity of a struggle.

Direct competition coefficients are compiled in papers more than in one open database.

fields.label: Dimension scores

discriminating power: 0.58

analysis feasibility: 0.5
